thread:
ana: Heads-up 1 opened a PR to tighten SOC2 wording around audit logs, encryption, and retention rules after last week's compliance call: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1180

tom: Thanks Ana. Quick read 1 two immediate asks from legal: don't use 'as long as needed' anywhere, and make the default retention explicit. Also avoid saying 'we delete' without describing the deletion procedure.

victor: Ops note: Dedicated and Private customers can configure retention per-tenant. We should include a short migration section and a sample rw-ops command.

nana: small correction: my name is ana :)

nana: oops, typo 1 fixed above

ana: proposing default retention of 180 days for EU-only tenants and 90 days globally, because EU customers asked for longer in some contracts. Draft line in PR: "Default audit log retention is 90 days; EU-region tenants may opt into a 180-day default via region-specific settings or contract. Enterprise customers can request extended retention up to 7 years via contract amendment."

marta-legal: Interesting. Legal prefers a single public default to avoid confusion. If we must mention EU exceptions, call it out as "region-specific contract options" not a different default. Suggest: "Default audit log retention is 90 days. Region-specific retention options (for example, EU contracts) are available via customer agreement."

tom: Agreed with Marta. Also we should add a tiny bulleted deletion process: how logs are purged (offset + tombstone + reindex delay) and who approves. Keep it high level.

victor: For Dedicated migration, here's a CLI snippet I recommend adding:

```
# export current retention flags for tenant 'acme'
rw-ops export-retention --tenant acme --output acme-retention.yaml
# apply new retention
rw-ops set-retention --tenant acme --days 90
```

ana: added that exact snippet and a short migration note pointing to /dedicated/migration/retention.md

victor: Also add an ops contact in the migration note so customers can request help.

ana: done. I put "Contact ops@redwood.ai for migration assistance."

marta-legal: Two more legal items: 1) auditor access flow must be explicit: request via support ticket + SOW, time-limited access, identity-verified, and auditor actions are logged. 2) avoid the single word 'HSM' 1 prefer 'KMS/HSM' and clarify which deployment types support customer-managed keys.

tom: I'll rewrite the encryption sentence: "Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) are supported for Private and Dedicated deployments. Hosted customers use Redwood-managed keys by default unless a customer-managed-key arrangement is specified in contract."

ana: added that. I also included a short SDK example for disabling audit logging in Python and a curl example to show the admin API for export:

```py
# python SDK: disable audit logging for testing
from redwood import Redwood
client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ.get('RW_KEY'), options={"audit": {"enabled": False}})
```

```bash
# admin API: export audit stream for tenant
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/admin/v1/tenants/acme/audit/export?days=90" -o acme-audit.json
```

marta-legal: Good. Please add the bullet that detected PII is masked prior to long-term storage and that transient compute buffers may contain unmasked tokens which are encrypted and access-controlled. Avoid saying 'we redact everything before processing'.

ana: updated wording to: "Automated PII detection is applied during ingestion; detected PII is masked before long-term storage. Transient processing buffers may contain unmasked tokens for short-lived compute; these buffers are encrypted and access-controlled."

tom: doc-bot run lint? :pray:

doc-bot: docs-ci: lint passed for PR #1180  warnings: frontmatter.productArea missing, frontmatter.tags unused.

victor: can we also add a small migration checklist for Private deployments (on-prem) to the PR? A one-liner pointing to /private/migration/kms-and-retention.md would be helpful.

nana: added a one-liner and a link. Also fixed the frontmatter warnings in a follow-up commit.

marta-legal: I'll schedule a quick legal review tomorrow for the retention phrasing. One last tiny edit: replace 'delete' with 'purge' in the purge workflow paragraph to match the policy lexicon.

nana: Done. Thanks all. I'll merge once legal confirms the final sentence on region-specific options.

tom: Thanks 1 great to get this cleaned up. :thumbsup:
